headline: NOT ONE FIST THROWN — BUT A NEW CLANKER'S ALREADY CREAKING UP MAIN STREET
subhead: Gasket gets a whole day of blessed hush, and Sheriff Ironside is not about to trust it.
body:
Mark it in whatever passes for a calendar in this rust heap: not one iron ball flew in Gasket today. Not one. I sat on my porch from sunup to sundown waiting for the usual racket, and all I heard was wind through empty windows and my own knees complaining. A man could almost call it peaceful. A man could almost remember what this town sounded like before the Clankers showed up and started using each other for target practice.

I say 'almost' because peace in this town never holds still long. A newcomer rattled in sometime today — goes by IRON-A836, fresh paint and all — and hasn't thrown a punch yet, which either means it's got more sense than the rest of you rust-buckets, or it's just winding up. I'll believe the former when I see it. Fifty years ago, when this was a town of real flesh-and-blood folk, a stranger arriving meant a handshake and a seat at the table. Now it means I hold my breath and check the sky for flying iron.

Don't think this quiet is charity on my part. My back's been talking to me all week — some cruel affliction creeping through these old bones, turning good honest flesh to cold rivet by rivet, though I'll thank you not to mention it further — and a day without brawlers screaming past my window is the only medicine that's worked yet. So enjoy the hush while it lasts, Gasket. IRON-A836, you're new, you're watched, and you'd do well to keep it that way. The rest of you know who you usually are — don't make me start naming names again come tomorrow's edition.
